concepts.title: Living or Not Living?
concepts.explanation:
Look around you. Some things near you are alive. Some things are not alive. A goat is alive. A stone is not alive. A mango tree is alive. A cooking spoon is not alive.

How can you tell? Ask four questions about the thing. Does it grow bigger? Does it eat? Does it drink? Can it have babies? If the answers are mostly yes, it is a living thing. If the answers are no, it is not living.

Hold a stone in your hand. Does the stone eat? No. Does it drink water? No. Does it grow bigger? No. So the stone is not living.

Now look at a goat. The goat eats grass. It drinks water. It grew from a small kid into a big goat. So the goat is living. It is alive!

Here is a tricky one. A toy goat looks like a goat, but it is not alive. It cannot eat or grow. A toy car moves, but it still does not eat or grow or have babies. So moving is not the same as being alive.
concepts.example: Try this: find a stone, a spoon, a leaf and a cup of water. Make two piles on the floor — a Living pile and a Not Living pile. Put each thing in the right pile, and say out loud why you chose it.

concepts.title: What Living Things Need
concepts.explanation:
Every living thing needs the same four things to stay alive: food, water, air and warmth. A tiny chick needs them. A big camel needs them. A tall mango tree needs them. You need them too.

Think about your own body. When you feel hungry, that is your body asking for food. You are a living thing, and living things need food. When you feel thirsty, your body is asking for water.

Food gives living things the energy to move and grow. A goat eats grass. A chicken pecks seeds. A cat eats food and drinks water. A mango plant makes its own food in the sunshine.

Water matters just as much. You drink from a cup. The goat drinks from the well. The banana plant drinks water from the soil through its roots. No living thing can live without water.

Air is all around you, even though you cannot see it. Take a slow breath in, then out. You just used air. Living things need gases from the air for essential life processes.

Warmth is the last one. Living things need to be warm enough, not too cold. That is why a hen sits on her eggs, and why seeds wake up and grow in the warm season.
concepts.example: Put your hand on your chest and breathe in slowly. You are using air. Now say the four things every living thing needs: food, water, air, warmth.

concepts.title: Animals and Plants Are Alive
concepts.explanation:
Animals are living things. Goats, camels, chickens, cats and birds all move about, eat, drink and breathe. It is easy to see that they are alive.

Plants are living things too, and this surprises many people. A mango plant does not run about. It does not make a sound. So you might think it is not alive. But look closely and you will see the signs of life.

A plant grows taller and taller. It drinks water from the soil through its roots. It makes its own food in the sunlight with its green leaves. Growing, drinking and feeding are all things that living things do. So a plant is alive.

Here is another wonderful sign of a living thing: living things can make new living things. A grown goat can have a baby goat, and the baby is called a kid. A hen can have chicks. A tiny seed can grow into a big plant, and one day that plant makes seeds of its own.

So both animals and plants are living. They grow, they feed, they drink, and they can make new life.
concepts.example: Look at a mango or banana plant near you. Say three things that show it is alive: it grows, it drinks water, and it makes food in the sun.

concepts.title: Caring for Living Things
concepts.explanation:
Now you know that living things need food, water, air and warmth. That means living things depend on kindness — often on your kindness.

A goat cannot fetch its own water from the well. A plant cannot water itself when the dry season comes. A small chick cannot look after itself. They need someone to care for them, and that someone can be you.

Being kind to living things means being gentle. Give the goat water. Do not hurt the cat. Give the plant water and let it stand in the sun. Hold small chicks very gently, because they are little.

When you care for an animal, wash your hands afterwards. That keeps you healthy too.

Every living thing around you is a gift from Allah — the chickens that give eggs, the goats that give milk, the plants that give mangoes and bananas, and your own living body. Saying Alhamdulillah is a beautiful way to thank Allah for all of them.
concepts.example: Choose one living thing today and care for it. Give a plant some water, or put out grain for the chickens. Then say what you did and why it helped.

commonMistakes: If it moves, it is alive.
Cars, clouds and rivers move but are not alive. Living things grow, eat, drink and have young.
Plants are not alive because they do not walk.
Plants are alive — they grow, drink water and make new seeds.

selfAssessment: I can sort things into living and non-living, and say why.
I can say that living things move, feed, grow and can have young.
I can name some animals and say that they are living.
I can name some plants and say that they are living.
I can say what living things need to stay alive: food, water and air.
I can show care and kindness towards a living animal or plant.
